ar.question: كم زوجاً مرتباً من الأعداد الصحيحة \( (a, b) \) حيث \( 1 \le a \le 15 \) و\( 1 \le b \le 15 \) يحقق أن \( a^2 + b^2 \) يقبل القسمة على \( 3 \)؟
ar.hint: اكتب جميع بواقي المربعات الممكنة عند القسمة على 3: {0, 1}! أي باقيين منها فقط يمكن أن يكون مجموعهما مضاعفاً لـ 3؟
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عند القسمة على \( 3 \)، البواقي الممكنة لأي مربع كامل \( x^2 \) هي فقط \( \{0, 1\} \)، ولا يوجد أي باقيين غير صفريين منها مجموعهما يساوي \( 3 \)!

الخطوة 1: بفحص الأزواج من \( \{0, 1\} \) نجد أن الحالة الوحيدة لقسمة \( a^2 + b^2 \) على \( 3 \) هي \( 0 + 0 \)، أي يجب أن يكون كلٌّ من \( a \) و\( b \) من مضاعفات \( 3 \)!

الخطوة 2: في المدى من \( 1 \) إلى \( 15 \) يوجد \( \lfloor 15/3 \rfloor = 5 \) مضاعفاً للعدد \( 3 \).

الخطوة 3: عدد الأزواج المرتبة \( (a, b) \) هو: \( 5 \times 5 = 25 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: قاعدة ذهبية في نظرية الأعداد: لقسمة مجموع مربعين على عدد أولي يترك باقي 3 عند قسمته على 4 (مثل 3 و7 و11)، يجب أن يقسم العدد الأولي كلا العددين معاً!

en.question: How many ordered pairs of integers \( (a, b) \) with \( 1 \le a \le 25 \) and \( 1 \le b \le 25 \) have the property that \( a^2 + b^2 \) is divisible by \( 3 \)?
en.hint: List all possible remainders of a² when divided by 3: {0, 1}! Which two remainders from this list can add up to a multiple of 3?
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Modulo \( 3 \), the only possible remainders of a square \( x^2 \) are \( \{0, 1\} \). Notice that NO two non-zero remainders in that set add up to \( 3 \)!

Step 1: Test all pairs from \( \{0, 1\} \): the only way \( a^2 + b^2 \equiv 0 \pmod{3} \) is \( 0 + 0 \equiv 0 \), meaning both \( a \) and \( b \) must be multiples of \( 3 \)!

Step 2: Between \( 1 \) and \( 25 \), there are \( \lfloor 25/3 \rfloor = 8 \) multiples of \( 3 \).

Step 3: Choose \( a \) in \( 8 \) ways and \( b \) independently in \( 8 \) ways: \( 8 \times 8 = 64 \) ordered pairs.

✅ Quick Check: Checked across all \( 625 \) pairs in \( \{1..25\}^2 \): \( 64 \) pairs work!

ar.question: كم زوجاً مرتباً من الأعداد الصحيحة \( (a, b) \) حيث \( 1 \le a \le 25 \) و\( 1 \le b \le 25 \) يحقق أن \( a^2 + b^2 \) يقبل القسمة على \( 7 \)؟
ar.hint: اكتب جميع بواقي المربعات الممكنة عند القسمة على 7: {0, 1, 2, 4}! أي باقيين منها فقط يمكن أن يكون مجموعهما مضاعفاً لـ 7؟
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عند القسمة على \( 7 \)، البواقي الممكنة لأي مربع كامل \( x^2 \) هي فقط \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \)، ولا يوجد أي باقيين غير صفريين منها مجموعهما يساوي \( 7 \)!

الخطوة 1: بفحص الأزواج من \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \) نجد أن الحالة الوحيدة لقسمة \( a^2 + b^2 \) على \( 7 \) هي \( 0 + 0 \)، أي يجب أن يكون كلٌّ من \( a \) و\( b \) من مضاعفات \( 7 \)!

الخطوة 2: في المدى من \( 1 \) إلى \( 25 \) يوجد \( \lfloor 25/7 \rfloor = 3 \) مضاعفاً للعدد \( 7 \).

الخطوة 3: عدد الأزواج المرتبة \( (a, b) \) هو: \( 3 \times 3 = 9 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: قاعدة ذهبية في نظرية الأعداد: لقسمة مجموع مربعين على عدد أولي يترك باقي 3 عند قسمته على 4 (مثل 3 و7 و11)، يجب أن يقسم العدد الأولي كلا العددين معاً!

en.question: How many ordered pairs of integers \( (a, b) \) with \( 1 \le a \le 40 \) and \( 1 \le b \le 40 \) have the property that \( a^2 + b^2 \) is divisible by \( 7 \)?
en.hint: List all possible remainders of a² when divided by 7: {0, 1, 2, 4}! Which two remainders from this list can add up to a multiple of 7?
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Modulo \( 7 \), the only possible remainders of a square \( x^2 \) are \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \). Notice that NO two non-zero remainders in that set add up to \( 7 \)!

Step 1: Test all pairs from \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \): the only way \( a^2 + b^2 \equiv 0 \pmod{7} \) is \( 0 + 0 \equiv 0 \), meaning both \( a \) and \( b \) must be multiples of \( 7 \)!

Step 2: Between \( 1 \) and \( 40 \), there are \( \lfloor 40/7 \rfloor = 5 \) multiples of \( 7 \).

Step 3: Choose \( a \) in \( 5 \) ways and \( b \) independently in \( 5 \) ways: \( 5 \times 5 = 25 \) ordered pairs.

✅ Quick Check: Checked across all \( 1600 \) pairs in \( \{1..40\}^2 \): \( 25 \) pairs work!

en.hint: List all possible remainders of a² when divided by 7: {0, 1, 2, 4}! Which two remainders from this list can add up to a multiple of 7?
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Modulo \( 7 \), the only possible remainders of a square \( x^2 \) are \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \). Notice that NO two non-zero remainders in that set add up to \( 7 \)!

Step 1: Test all pairs from \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \): the only way \( a^2 + b^2 \equiv 0 \pmod{7} \) is \( 0 + 0 \equiv 0 \), meaning both \( a \) and \( b \) must be multiples of \( 7 \)!

Step 2: Between \( 1 \) and \( 70 \), there are \( \lfloor 70/7 \rfloor = 10 \) multiples of \( 7 \).

Step 3: Choose \( a \) in \( 10 \) ways and \( b \) independently in \( 10 \) ways: \( 10 \times 10 = 100 \) ordered pairs.

✅ Quick Check: Checked across all \( 4900 \) pairs in \( \{1..70\}^2 \): \( 100 \) pairs work!

ar.question: كم زوجاً مرتباً من الأعداد الصحيحة \( (a, b) \) حيث \( 1 \le a \le 70 \) و\( 1 \le b \le 70 \) يحقق أن \( a^2 + b^2 \) يقبل القسمة على \( 7 \)؟
ar.hint: اكتب جميع بواقي المربعات الممكنة عند القسمة على 7: {0, 1, 2, 4}! أي باقيين منها فقط يمكن أن يكون مجموعهما مضاعفاً لـ 7؟
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عند القسمة على \( 7 \)، البواقي الممكنة لأي مربع كامل \( x^2 \) هي فقط \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \)، ولا يوجد أي باقيين غير صفريين منها مجموعهما يساوي \( 7 \)!

الخطوة 1: بفحص الأزواج من \( \{0, 1, 2, 4\} \) نجد أن الحالة الوحيدة لقسمة \( a^2 + b^2 \) على \( 7 \) هي \( 0 + 0 \)، أي يجب أن يكون كلٌّ من \( a \) و\( b \) من مضاعفات \( 7 \)!

الخطوة 2: في المدى من \( 1 \) إلى \( 70 \) يوجد \( \lfloor 70/7 \rfloor = 10 \) مضاعفاً للعدد \( 7 \).

الخطوة 3: عدد الأزواج المرتبة \( (a, b) \) هو: \( 10 \times 10 = 100 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: قاعدة ذهبية في نظرية الأعداد: لقسمة مجموع مربعين على عدد أولي يترك باقي 3 عند قسمته على 4 (مثل 3 و7 و11)، يجب أن يقسم العدد الأولي كلا العددين معاً!

en.question: How many ordered pairs of integers \( (a, b) \) with \( 1 \le a \le 100 \) and \( 1 \le b \le 100 \) have the property that \( a^2 + b^2 \) is divisible by \( 11 \)?
en.hint: List all possible remainders of a² when divided by 11: {0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9}! Which two remainders from this list can add up to a multiple of 11?
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Modulo \( 11 \), the only possible remainders of a square \( x^2 \) are \( \{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9\} \). Notice that NO two non-zero remainders in that set add up to \( 11 \)!

Step 1: Test all pairs from \( \{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9\} \): the only way \( a^2 + b^2 \equiv 0 \pmod{11} \) is \( 0 + 0 \equiv 0 \), meaning both \( a \) and \( b \) must be multiples of \( 11 \)!

Step 2: Between \( 1 \) and \( 100 \), there are \( \lfloor 100/11 \rfloor = 9 \) multiples of \( 11 \).

Step 3: Choose \( a \) in \( 9 \) ways and \( b \) independently in \( 9 \) ways: \( 9 \times 9 = 81 \) ordered pairs.

✅ Quick Check: Checked across all \( 10000 \) pairs in \( \{1..100\}^2 \): \( 81 \) pairs work!

ar.question: كم زوجاً مرتباً من الأعداد الصحيحة \( (a, b) \) حيث \( 1 \le a \le 100 \) و\( 1 \le b \le 100 \) يحقق أن \( a^2 + b^2 \) يقبل القسمة على \( 11 \)؟
ar.hint: اكتب جميع بواقي المربعات الممكنة عند القسمة على 11: {0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9}! أي باقيين منها فقط يمكن أن يكون مجموعهما مضاعفاً لـ 11؟
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عند القسمة على \( 11 \)، البواقي الممكنة لأي مربع كامل \( x^2 \) هي فقط \( \{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9\} \)، ولا يوجد أي باقيين غير صفريين منها مجموعهما يساوي \( 11 \)!

الخطوة 1: بفحص الأزواج من \( \{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 9\} \) نجد أن الحالة الوحيدة لقسمة \( a^2 + b^2 \) على \( 11 \) هي \( 0 + 0 \)، أي يجب أن يكون كلٌّ من \( a \) و\( b \) من مضاعفات \( 11 \)!

الخطوة 2: في المدى من \( 1 \) إلى \( 100 \) يوجد \( \lfloor 100/11 \rfloor = 9 \) مضاعفاً للعدد \( 11 \).

الخطوة 3: عدد الأزواج المرتبة \( (a, b) \) هو: \( 9 \times 9 = 81 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: قاعدة ذهبية في نظرية الأعداد: لقسمة مجموع مربعين على عدد أولي يترك باقي 3 عند قسمته على 4 (مثل 3 و7 و11)، يجب أن يقسم العدد الأولي كلا العددين معاً!

en.question: What is the exact value of \( \frac{2^{-2} + 5^0}{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2}} \)?
en.hint: Use three basic exponent rules step by step: 5⁰ = 1, 2⁻² = 1/4, and (2/3)⁻² = (3/2)²!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Recall the three rules of zero and negative exponents: \( x^0 = 1 \) (for \( x \ne 0 \)), \( x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n} \), and \( \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^n \).

Step 1: Simplify the numerator: \( 2^{-2} + 5^0 = \frac{1}{4} + 1 = \frac{5}{4} \).

Step 2: Simplify the denominator by flipping the fraction: \( \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4} \).

Step 3: Divide numerator by denominator (the \( 4 \) denominators cancel!): \( \frac{5}{4} \div \frac{9}{4} = \frac{5}{9} \).

✅ Quick Check: Common trap avoided: \( 5^0 = 1 \), NOT \( 0 \)!

ar.question: ما القيمة الدقيقة للمقدار \( \frac{2^{-2} + 5^0}{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2}} \)؟
ar.hint: استخدم ثلاث قواعد أساسية للأسس خطوة بخطوة: 5⁰ = 1، و2⁻² = 1/4، و(2/3)⁻² = (3/2)²!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نتذكر قواعد الأس الصفري والأس السالب: \( x^0 = 1 \)، و\( x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n} \)، و\( \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^n \).

الخطوة 1: نبسّط البسط: \( 2^{-2} + 5^0 = \frac{1}{4} + 1 = \frac{5}{4} \).

الخطوة 2: نبسّط المقام بقلب الكسر وتغيير إشارة الأس: \( \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4} \).

الخطوة 3: نقسم البسط على المقام (يُختصر المقام \( 4 \) في كليهما!): \( \frac{5}{9} = \frac{5}{9} \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تجنبنا الخطأ الشائع: \( 5^0 = 1 \) وليس \( 0 \)!

en.question: What is the exact value of \( \frac{2^{-2} + 9^0}{\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-2}} \)?
en.hint: Use three basic exponent rules step by step: 9⁰ = 1, 2⁻² = 1/4, and (2/5)⁻² = (5/2)²!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Recall the three rules of zero and negative exponents: \( x^0 = 1 \) (for \( x \ne 0 \)), \( x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n} \), and \( \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^n \).

Step 1: Simplify the numerator: \( 2^{-2} + 9^0 = \frac{1}{4} + 1 = \frac{5}{4} \).

Step 2: Simplify the denominator by flipping the fraction: \( \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{4} \).

Step 3: Divide numerator by denominator (the \( 4 \) denominators cancel!): \( \frac{5}{4} \div \frac{25}{4} = \frac{1}{5} \).

✅ Quick Check: Common trap avoided: \( 9^0 = 1 \), NOT \( 0 \)!

en.question: What is the exact value of \( \frac{5^{-2} + 4^0}{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^{-2}} \)?
en.hint: Use three basic exponent rules step by step: 4⁰ = 1, 5⁻² = 1/25, and (5/2)⁻² = (2/5)²!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Recall the three rules of zero and negative exponents: \( x^0 = 1 \) (for \( x \ne 0 \)), \( x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n} \), and \( \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^n \).

Step 1: Simplify the numerator: \( 5^{-2} + 4^0 = \frac{1}{25} + 1 = \frac{26}{25} \).

Step 2: Simplify the denominator by flipping the fraction: \( \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{25} \).

Step 3: Divide numerator by denominator (the \( 25 \) denominators cancel!): \( \frac{26}{25} \div \frac{4}{25} = \frac{13}{2} \).

✅ Quick Check: Common trap avoided: \( 4^0 = 1 \), NOT \( 0 \)!

en.question: Let \( F(x) = x^2 + 2 \) and \( G(x) = 3x - 1 \). If a new function \( H \) is defined by \( H(x) = F(x + 2) + G(x - 2) \), what is the value of \( H(1) \)?
en.hint: Don't expand F(x+2) algebraically! Just plug x = 1 directly into the parentheses first: x+2 = 3 and x−2 = -1!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = 1 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(1) = F(1 + 2) + G(1 - 2) = F(3) + G(-1) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(3) = 1(3)^2 + (2) = 11 \) and \( G(-1) = 3(-1) + (-1) = -4 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 11 + (-4) = 7 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (3)^2 = 9 \ge 0 \) always!

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (3)^2 = 9 \ge 0 \) always!

en.question: Let \( F(x) = 2x^2 + 3 \) and \( G(x) = 5x - 4 \). If a new function \( H \) is defined by \( H(x) = F(x + 2) + G(x - 2) \), what is the value of \( H(2) \)?
en.hint: Don't expand F(x+2) algebraically! Just plug x = 2 directly into the parentheses first: x+2 = 4 and x−2 = 0!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = 2 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(2) = F(2 + 2) + G(2 - 2) = F(4) + G(0) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(4) = 2(4)^2 + (3) = 35 \) and \( G(0) = 5(0) + (-4) = -4 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 35 + (-4) = 31 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (4)^2 = 16 \ge 0 \) always!

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بدلاً من فكّ الأقواس جبرياً بدلالة \( x \)، نحسب المدخلات العددية داخل الأقواس أولاً؛ فهذا أسرع ويمنع أخطاء الإشارات!

الخطوة 1: نعوض \( x = 2 \) في تعريف \( H(x) \): \( H(2) = F(2 + 2) + G(2 - 2) = F(4) + G(0) \).

الخطوة 2: نحسب كل دالة على حدة: \( F(4) = 35 \) و\( G(0) = -4 \).

الخطوة 3: نجمع القيمتين: \( 35 + (-4) = 31 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: انتبه للإشارات عند التربيع: \( (4)^2 = 16 \) موجب دائماً!

en.hint: Don't expand F(x+1) algebraically! Just plug x = 3 directly into the parentheses first: x+1 = 4 and x−1 = 2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = 3 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(3) = F(3 + 1) + G(3 - 1) = F(4) + G(2) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(4) = 3(4)^2 + (-2) = 46 \) and \( G(2) = -4(2) + (6) = -2 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 46 + (-2) = 44 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (4)^2 = 16 \ge 0 \) always!

en.hint: Don't expand F(x+4) algebraically! Just plug x = -1 directly into the parentheses first: x+4 = 3 and x−4 = -5!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = -1 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(-1) = F(-1 + 4) + G(-1 - 4) = F(3) + G(-5) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(3) = 1(3)^2 + (-3) = 6 \) and \( G(-5) = 6(-5) + (2) = -28 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 6 + (-28) = -22 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (3)^2 = 9 \ge 0 \) always!

الخطوة 1: نعوض \( x = -1 \) في تعريف \( H(x) \): \( H(-1) = F(-1 + 4) + G(-1 - 4) = F(3) + G(-5) \).

الخطوة 3: نجمع القيمتين: \( 6 + (-28) = -22 \).

en.question: Let \( F(x) = 2x^2 + 1 \) and \( G(x) = -3x + 8 \). If a new function \( H \) is defined by \( H(x) = F(x + 3) + G(x - 3) \), what is the value of \( H(-1) \)?
en.hint: Don't expand F(x+3) algebraically! Just plug x = -1 directly into the parentheses first: x+3 = 2 and x−3 = -4!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = -1 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(-1) = F(-1 + 3) + G(-1 - 3) = F(2) + G(-4) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(2) = 2(2)^2 + (1) = 9 \) and \( G(-4) = -3(-4) + (8) = 20 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 9 + (20) = 29 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (2)^2 = 4 \ge 0 \) always!

en.question: Let \( F(x) = 3x^2 + 4 \) and \( G(x) = 2x - 5 \). If a new function \( H \) is defined by \( H(x) = F(x + 2) + G(x - 2) \), what is the value of \( H(-3) \)?
en.hint: Don't expand F(x+2) algebraically! Just plug x = -3 directly into the parentheses first: x+2 = -1 and x−2 = -5!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = -3 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(-3) = F(-3 + 2) + G(-3 - 2) = F(-1) + G(-5) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(-1) = 3(-1)^2 + (4) = 7 \) and \( G(-5) = 2(-5) + (-5) = -15 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 7 + (-15) = -8 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (-1)^2 = 1 \ge 0 \) always!

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(6) = 2(6)^2 + (-5) = 67 \) and \( G(-2) = 7(-2) + (-3) = -17 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 67 + (-17) = 50 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (6)^2 = 36 \ge 0 \) always!

ar.question: لتكن \( F(x) = 2x^2 - 5 \) و\( G(x) = 7x - 3 \). إذا عُرِّفت الدالة \( H \) بالعلاقة \( H(x) = F(x + 4) + G(x - 4) \)، فما قيمة \( H(2) \)؟
ar.hint: لا تفكّ الأقواس جبرياً! عوّض مباشرة بـ x = 2 داخل القوسين أولاً: x+4 = 6 وx−4 = -2!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بدلاً من فكّ الأقواس جبرياً بدلالة \( x \)، نحسب المدخلات العددية داخل الأقواس أولاً؛ فهذا أسرع ويمنع أخطاء الإشارات!

الخطوة 1: نعوض \( x = 2 \) في تعريف \( H(x) \): \( H(2) = F(2 + 4) + G(2 - 4) = F(6) + G(-2) \).

الخطوة 2: نحسب كل دالة على حدة: \( F(6) = 67 \) و\( G(-2) = -17 \).

الخطوة 3: نجمع القيمتين: \( 67 + (-17) = 50 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: انتبه للإشارات عند التربيع: \( (6)^2 = 36 \) موجب دائماً!

en.question: Let \( F(x) = 3x^2 - 4 \) and \( G(x) = -5x + 9 \). If a new function \( H \) is defined by \( H(x) = F(x + 3) + G(x - 3) \), what is the value of \( H(2) \)?
en.hint: Don't expand F(x+3) algebraically! Just plug x = 2 directly into the parentheses first: x+3 = 5 and x−3 = -1!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of expanding formulas in \( x \), evaluate the shifted inputs numerically first — it is faster and avoids sign errors!

Step 1: Substitute \( x = 2 \) into \( H(x) \): \( H(2) = F(2 + 3) + G(2 - 3) = F(5) + G(-1) \).

Step 2: Compute each value: \( F(5) = 3(5)^2 + (-4) = 71 \) and \( G(-1) = -5(-1) + (9) = 14 \).

Step 3: Add them together: \( 71 + (14) = 85 \).

✅ Quick Check: Watch the signs when squaring: \( (5)^2 = 25 \ge 0 \) always!

en.question: Positive real numbers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfy \( x^2 + xy = 40 \) and \( xy + y^2 = 24 \). What is the value of \( x + y \)?
en.hint: Add the two equations together and look at the left-hand side: x² + 2xy + y² is a famous perfect square!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding both equations forms the perfect square identity \( (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2 \)!

Step 1: Add the two equations: \( (x^2 + xy) + (xy + y^2) = 40 + 24 = 64 \).

Step 2: Rewrite the left side as a square: \( x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2 = 64 \).

Step 3: Since \( x, y > 0 \), we have \( x + y > 0 \), so \( x + y = \sqrt{64} = 8 \).

✅ Quick Check: Bonus check: \( x(x+y)=40 \implies x=5 \) and \( y(x+y)=24 \implies y=3 \), which indeed satisfy both equations!

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق إضافي: \( x=5 \) و\( y=3 \) يحققان كلتا المعادلتين ومجموعهما \( 8 \).

الخطوة 1: نجمع المعادلتين طرفاً لطرف: \( (x^2 + xy) + (xy + y^2) = 60 + 40 = 100 \).

الخطوة 2: نكتب الطرف الأيسر كمربع كامل: \( x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2 = 100 \).

en.question: Positive real numbers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfy \( x^2 + xy = 84 \) and \( xy + y^2 = 60 \). What is the value of \( x + y \)?
en.hint: Add the two equations together and look at the left-hand side: x² + 2xy + y² is a famous perfect square!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding both equations forms the perfect square identity \( (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2 \)!

Step 1: Add the two equations: \( (x^2 + xy) + (xy + y^2) = 84 + 60 = 144 \).

Step 2: Rewrite the left side as a square: \( x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2 = 144 \).

Step 3: Since \( x, y > 0 \), we have \( x + y > 0 \), so \( x + y = \sqrt{144} = 12 \).

✅ Quick Check: Bonus check: \( x(x+y)=84 \implies x=7 \) and \( y(x+y)=60 \implies y=5 \), which indeed satisfy both equations!

ar.question: عددان حقيقيان موجبان \( x \) و\( y \) يحققان \( x^2 + xy = 198 \) و\( xy + y^2 = 126 \). ما قيمة \( x + y \)؟
ar.hint: اجمع المعادلتين معاً وتأمل الطرف الأيسر: المقدار x² + 2xy + y² مربع كامل مشهور!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: جمع المعادلتين يكوّن مباشرة متطابقة المربع الكامل \( (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2 \)!

الخطوة 1: نجمع المعادلتين طرفاً لطرف: \( (x^2 + xy) + (xy + y^2) = 198 + 126 = 324 \).

الخطوة 2: نكتب الطرف الأيسر كمربع كامل: \( x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2 = 324 \).

الخطوة 3: بما أن \( x, y > 0 \) فإن \( x + y > 0 \)، ومنه \( x + y = \sqrt{324} = 18 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق إضافي: \( x=11 \) و\( y=7 \) يحققان كلتا المعادلتين ومجموعهما \( 18 \).

en.question: Real numbers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfy \( x + y = 6 \) and \( x^3 + y^3 = 72 \). What is the value of the product \( xy \)?
en.hint: Cube (x + y): remember (x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the cube-of-a-sum identity \( (x + y)^3 = x^3 + y^3 + 3xy(x + y) \) so you never have to solve for \( x \) and \( y \) individually!

Step 1: Cube \( x + y = 6 \): \( (x + y)^3 = 6^3 = 216 \).

Step 2: Substitute \( x^3 + y^3 = 72 \) and \( x + y = 6 \) into \( (x+y)^3 = (x^3+y^3) + 3xy(x+y) \): \( 216 = 72 + 3(6)xy \).

Step 3: Solve for \( xy \): \( 18xy = 144 \implies xy = \frac{144}{18} = 8 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check with \( x = 4, y = 2 \): \( 4 + 2 = 6 \), \( 4^3 + 2^3 = 72 \), and \( xy = 8 \)!

en.question: Real numbers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfy \( x + y = 10 \) and \( x^3 + y^3 = 370 \). What is the value of the product \( xy \)?
en.hint: Cube (x + y): remember (x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the cube-of-a-sum identity \( (x + y)^3 = x^3 + y^3 + 3xy(x + y) \) so you never have to solve for \( x \) and \( y \) individually!

Step 1: Cube \( x + y = 10 \): \( (x + y)^3 = 10^3 = 1000 \).

Step 2: Substitute \( x^3 + y^3 = 370 \) and \( x + y = 10 \) into \( (x+y)^3 = (x^3+y^3) + 3xy(x+y) \): \( 1000 = 370 + 3(10)xy \).

Step 3: Solve for \( xy \): \( 30xy = 630 \implies xy = \frac{630}{30} = 21 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check with \( x = 7, y = 3 \): \( 7 + 3 = 10 \), \( 7^3 + 3^3 = 370 \), and \( xy = 21 \)!

en.question: What is the real value of \( x \) that satisfies \( \sqrt{x + 4} + \sqrt{x - 4} = 4 \)?
en.hint: Clever shortcut: set A = √(x + 4) and B = √(x - 4). Then A + B = 4, and A² − B² = (x + 4) − (x - 4) = 8!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of messy repeated squaring, name the two roots \( A = \sqrt{x + 4} \) and \( B = \sqrt{x - 4} \) and use \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

Step 1: Notice that \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 4) - (x - 4) = 8 \) (the \( x \) cancels out!).

Step 2: Since \( A + B = 4 \) and \( (A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2 \), divide by \( 4 \): \( A - B = \frac{8}{4} = 2 \).

Step 3: Add \( A + B = 4 \) and \( A - B = 2 \): \( 2A = 6 \implies A = 3 \). Squaring \( \sqrt{x + 4} = 3 \) gives \( x + 4 = 9 \implies x = 5 \).

✅ Quick Check: Substitute \( x = 5 \) back into the original equation: \( \sqrt{9} + \sqrt{1} = 3 + 1 = 4 \) — verified!

ar.question: ما قيمة العدد الحقيقي \( x \) الذي يحقق المعادلة \( \sqrt{x + 4} + \sqrt{x - 4} = 4 \)؟
ar.hint: اختصار ذكي: ضع A = √(x + 4) وB = √(x - 4)؛ فيكون A + B = 4، والفرق بين مربعيهما A² − B² = 8!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بدلاً من التربيع المتكرر المعقد، نرمز للجذرين بـ \( A = \sqrt{x + 4} \) و\( B = \sqrt{x - 4} \) ونستخدم متطابقة الفرق بين مربعين \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ أن \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 4) - (x - 4) = 8 \) (تختفي \( x \) تماماً!).

الخطوة 2: بما أن \( A + B = 4 \)، نقسم \( 8 \) على \( 4 \) فنحصل على \( A - B = \frac{8}{4} = 2 \).

الخطوة 3: بجمع المعادلتين نجد \( 2A = 6 \implies A = 3 \)، وبتربيع \( \sqrt{x + 4} = 3 \) نحصل على \( x + 4 = 9 \implies x = 5 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: التعويض للتحقق في المعادلة الأصلية: \( \sqrt{9} + \sqrt{1} = 3 + 1 = 4 \) — حل صحيح!

en.question: What is the real value of \( x \) that satisfies \( \sqrt{x + 9} + \sqrt{x - 3} = 6 \)?
en.hint: Clever shortcut: set A = √(x + 9) and B = √(x - 3). Then A + B = 6, and A² − B² = (x + 9) − (x - 3) = 12!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of messy repeated squaring, name the two roots \( A = \sqrt{x + 9} \) and \( B = \sqrt{x - 3} \) and use \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

Step 1: Notice that \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 9) - (x - 3) = 12 \) (the \( x \) cancels out!).

Step 2: Since \( A + B = 6 \) and \( (A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2 \), divide by \( 6 \): \( A - B = \frac{12}{6} = 2 \).

Step 3: Add \( A + B = 6 \) and \( A - B = 2 \): \( 2A = 8 \implies A = 4 \). Squaring \( \sqrt{x + 9} = 4 \) gives \( x + 9 = 16 \implies x = 7 \).

✅ Quick Check: Substitute \( x = 7 \) back into the original equation: \( \sqrt{16} + \sqrt{4} = 4 + 2 = 6 \) — verified!

en.question: What is the real value of \( x \) that satisfies \( \sqrt{x + 31} + \sqrt{x - 9} = 10 \)?
en.hint: Clever shortcut: set A = √(x + 31) and B = √(x - 9). Then A + B = 10, and A² − B² = (x + 31) − (x - 9) = 40!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of messy repeated squaring, name the two roots \( A = \sqrt{x + 31} \) and \( B = \sqrt{x - 9} \) and use \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

Step 1: Notice that \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 31) - (x - 9) = 40 \) (the \( x \) cancels out!).

Step 2: Since \( A + B = 10 \) and \( (A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2 \), divide by \( 10 \): \( A - B = \frac{40}{10} = 4 \).

Step 3: Add \( A + B = 10 \) and \( A - B = 4 \): \( 2A = 14 \implies A = 7 \). Squaring \( \sqrt{x + 31} = 7 \) gives \( x + 31 = 49 \implies x = 18 \).

✅ Quick Check: Substitute \( x = 18 \) back into the original equation: \( \sqrt{49} + \sqrt{9} = 7 + 3 = 10 \) — verified!

ar.question: ما قيمة العدد الحقيقي \( x \) الذي يحقق المعادلة \( \sqrt{x + 34} + \sqrt{x - 14} = 12 \)؟
ar.hint: اختصار ذكي: ضع A = √(x + 34) وB = √(x - 14)؛ فيكون A + B = 12، والفرق بين مربعيهما A² − B² = 48!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بدلاً من التربيع المتكرر المعقد، نرمز للجذرين بـ \( A = \sqrt{x + 34} \) و\( B = \sqrt{x - 14} \) ونستخدم متطابقة الفرق بين مربعين \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ أن \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 34) - (x - 14) = 48 \) (تختفي \( x \) تماماً!).

الخطوة 2: بما أن \( A + B = 12 \)، نقسم \( 48 \) على \( 12 \) فنحصل على \( A - B = \frac{48}{12} = 4 \).

الخطوة 3: بجمع المعادلتين نجد \( 2A = 16 \implies A = 8 \)، وبتربيع \( \sqrt{x + 34} = 8 \) نحصل على \( x + 34 = 64 \implies x = 30 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: التعويض للتحقق في المعادلة الأصلية: \( \sqrt{64} + \sqrt{16} = 8 + 4 = 12 \) — حل صحيح!

en.question: What is the real value of \( x \) that satisfies \( \sqrt{x + 41} + \sqrt{x - 15} = 14 \)?
en.hint: Clever shortcut: set A = √(x + 41) and B = √(x - 15). Then A + B = 14, and A² − B² = (x + 41) − (x - 15) = 56!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Instead of messy repeated squaring, name the two roots \( A = \sqrt{x + 41} \) and \( B = \sqrt{x - 15} \) and use \( A^2 - B^2 = (A - B)(A + B) \)!

Step 1: Notice that \( A^2 - B^2 = (x + 41) - (x - 15) = 56 \) (the \( x \) cancels out!).

Step 2: Since \( A + B = 14 \) and \( (A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2 \), divide by \( 14 \): \( A - B = \frac{56}{14} = 4 \).

Step 3: Add \( A + B = 14 \) and \( A - B = 4 \): \( 2A = 18 \implies A = 9 \). Squaring \( \sqrt{x + 41} = 9 \) gives \( x + 41 = 81 \implies x = 40 \).

✅ Quick Check: Substitute \( x = 40 \) back into the original equation: \( \sqrt{81} + \sqrt{25} = 9 + 5 = 14 \) — verified!

en.question: How many integers \( k \) satisfy the inequality \( (k + 3)(6 - k)(k - 2)^2 > 0 \)?
en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Squared factors never flip the sign of an inequality, but their root makes the whole product zero!

Step 1: Notice that the squared factor \( (k - 2)^2 \) is positive for every \( k \ne 2 \), and equals \( 0 \) when \( k = 2 \)!

Step 2: For \( k \ne 2 \), we need \( (k + 3)(6 - k) > 0 \), which holds strictly between the roots: \( -3 < k < 6 \).

Step 3: The integers in \( (-3, 6) \) run from \( -2 \) to \( 5 \) (\( 8 \) integers), minus \( k = 2 \) where the product is \( 0 \): \( 8 - 1 = 7 \) integers.

✅ Quick Check: Programmatic check over all integers confirms exactly \( 7 \) integer solutions.

ar.question: كم عدداً صحيحاً \( k \) يحقق المتباينة \( (k + 3)(6 - k)(k - 2)^2 > 0 \)؟
ar.hint: انتبه جيداً للعامل المربّع! فالمربع غير سالب دائماً، ويساوي صفراً عند جذره (فيُستبعد في حالة «< 0» ويُحسب ضمن الحلول في حالة «≤ 0»)!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: العوامل المربّعة لا تغيّر إشارة المتباينة أبداً، لكن جذرها يجعل حاصل الضرب الكلي مساوياً للصفر!

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ أن العامل المربّع \( (k - 2)^2 \) موجب دائماً لكل \( k \ne 2 \)، ويساوي \( 0 \) عند \( k = 2 \)!

الخطوة 2: لكي يكون الجداء موجباً تماماً (\( > 0 \)) يجب أن يكون \( (k + 3)(6 - k) > 0 \)، أي \( -3 < k < 6 \) مع استبعاد \( k = 2 \).

الخطوة 3: الأعداد الصحيحة من \( -2 \) إلى \( 5 \) عددها \( 8 \)، نطرح منها العدد \( k = 2 \) فيكون الناتج \( 7 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: بالتحقق من أطراف الفترة وجذر العامل المربّع نتأكد أن عدد الحلول الصحيحة هو \( 7 \) بالضبط.

en.question: How many integers \( k \) satisfy the inequality \( (k + 4)(5 - k)(k - 1)^2 > 0 \)?
en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!

ar.question: كم عدداً صحيحاً \( k \) يحقق المتباينة \( (k + 4)(5 - k)(k - 1)^2 > 0 \)؟
ar.hint: انتبه جيداً للعامل المربّع! فالمربع غير سالب دائماً، ويساوي صفراً عند جذره (فيُستبعد في حالة «< 0» ويُحسب ضمن الحلول في حالة «≤ 0»)!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: العوامل المربّعة لا تغيّر إشارة المتباينة أبداً، لكن جذرها يجعل حاصل الضرب الكلي مساوياً للصفر!

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ أن العامل المربّع \( (k - 1)^2 \) موجب دائماً لكل \( k \ne 1 \)، ويساوي \( 0 \) عند \( k = 1 \)!

الخطوة 2: لكي يكون الجداء موجباً تماماً (\( > 0 \)) يجب أن يكون \( (k + 4)(5 - k) > 0 \)، أي \( -4 < k < 5 \) مع استبعاد \( k = 1 \).

الخطوة 3: الأعداد الصحيحة من \( -3 \) إلى \( 4 \) عددها \( 8 \)، نطرح منها العدد \( k = 1 \) فيكون الناتج \( 7 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: بالتحقق من أطراف الفترة وجذر العامل المربّع نتأكد أن عدد الحلول الصحيحة هو \( 7 \) بالضبط.

en.question: How many integers \( k \) satisfy the inequality \( (k + 2)(8 - k)(k - 5)^2 > 0 \)?
en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!

💡 Key Idea: Squared factors never flip the sign of an inequality, but their root makes the whole product zero!

Step 3: The integers in \( (-2, 8) \) run from \( -1 \) to \( 7 \) (\( 9 \) integers), minus \( k = 5 \) where the product is \( 0 \): \( 9 - 1 = 8 \) integers.

✅ Quick Check: Programmatic check over all integers confirms exactly \( 8 \) integer solutions.

en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!

✅ Quick Check: Programmatic check over all integers confirms exactly \( 10 \) integer solutions.

ar.hint: انتبه جيداً للعامل المربّع! فالمربع غير سالب دائماً، ويساوي صفراً عند جذره (فيُستبعد في حالة «< 0» ويُحسب ضمن الحلول في حالة «≤ 0»)!

الخطوة 1: متى يكون \( (k + 3)(5 - k) \ge 0 \)؟ في الفترة المغلقة \( -3 \le k \le 5 \) التي تضم \( 5 - (-3) + 1 = 9 \) عدداً صحيحاً.

en.question: How many integers \( k \) satisfy the inequality \( (k + 8)(10 - k)(k - 4)^2 > 0 \)?
en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Squared factors never flip the sign of an inequality, but their root makes the whole product zero!

Step 1: Notice that the squared factor \( (k - 4)^2 \) is positive for every \( k \ne 4 \), and equals \( 0 \) when \( k = 4 \)!

Step 2: For \( k \ne 4 \), we need \( (k + 8)(10 - k) > 0 \), which holds strictly between the roots: \( -8 < k < 10 \).

Step 3: The integers in \( (-8, 10) \) run from \( -7 \) to \( 9 \) (\( 17 \) integers), minus \( k = 4 \) where the product is \( 0 \): \( 17 - 1 = 16 \) integers.

✅ Quick Check: Programmatic check over all integers confirms exactly \( 16 \) integer solutions.

ar.question: كم عدداً صحيحاً \( k \) يحقق المتباينة \( (k + 8)(10 - k)(k - 4)^2 > 0 \)؟
ar.hint: انتبه جيداً للعامل المربّع! فالمربع غير سالب دائماً، ويساوي صفراً عند جذره (فيُستبعد في حالة «< 0» ويُحسب ضمن الحلول في حالة «≤ 0»)!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: العوامل المربّعة لا تغيّر إشارة المتباينة أبداً، لكن جذرها يجعل حاصل الضرب الكلي مساوياً للصفر!

الخطوة 1: نلاحظ أن العامل المربّع \( (k - 4)^2 \) موجب دائماً لكل \( k \ne 4 \)، ويساوي \( 0 \) عند \( k = 4 \)!

الخطوة 2: لكي يكون الجداء موجباً تماماً (\( > 0 \)) يجب أن يكون \( (k + 8)(10 - k) > 0 \)، أي \( -8 < k < 10 \) مع استبعاد \( k = 4 \).

الخطوة 3: الأعداد الصحيحة من \( -7 \) إلى \( 9 \) عددها \( 17 \)، نطرح منها العدد \( k = 4 \) فيكون الناتج \( 16 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: بالتحقق من أطراف الفترة وجذر العامل المربّع نتأكد أن عدد الحلول الصحيحة هو \( 16 \) بالضبط.

en.question: How many integers \( k \) satisfy the inequality \( (k + 5)(9 - k)(k - 12)^2 \ge 0 \)?
en.hint: Watch the squared factor carefully! A square is ≥ 0 everywhere, and equals 0 at its root (which is EXCLUDED for '> 0' and INCLUDED for '≥ 0')!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Squared factors never flip the sign of an inequality, but their root makes the whole product zero!

Step 1: Where is \( (k + 5)(9 - k) \ge 0 \)? On the closed interval \( -5 \le k \le 9 \), which contains \( 9 - (-5) + 1 = 15 \) integers.

Step 2: WAIT — don't forget where the squared factor \( (k - 12)^2 \) equals zero! At \( k = 12 \) (outside \( [-5, 9] \)), the entire product equals \( 0 \ge 0 \)!

Step 3: Adding that isolated zero \( k = 12 \) gives \( 15 + 1 = 16 \) integers in total.

✅ Quick Check: Programmatic check over all integers confirms exactly \( 16 \) integer solutions.

en.question: What is the exact value of the sum \( \frac{1}{1\times2} + \frac{1}{2\times3} + \dots + \frac{1}{19\times20} \)?
en.hint: Rewrite each fraction using 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1) and watch almost every term cancel out!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the telescoping identity \( \frac{1}{k(k+1)} = \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \): every inner negative fraction cancels the next positive fraction!

Step 1: Split each term: \( \left(\frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \dots + \left(\frac{1}{19} - \frac{1}{20}\right) \).

Step 2: All middle terms cancel in pairs, leaving only the very first and very last pieces: \( \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{20} \).

Step 3: Combine over common denominator \( 20 \) and simplify: \( \frac{19}{20} \).

✅ Quick Check: Test with just 2 terms (\( \frac{1}{1(2)} + \frac{1}{(2)(3)} \)): the formula \( \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{3} \) works identically!

ar.hint: أعد كتابة كل كسر بالمتطابقة 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1) وستلاحظ شطب جميع الحدود الوسطى بالتعاقب!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستخدم المتطابقة التلسكوبية \( \frac{1}{k(k+1)} = \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \) حيث يُشطب كل حد سالب مع الحد الموجب الذي يليه!

الخطوة 1: نفكّك كل كسر: \( \left(\frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \dots + \left(\frac{1}{19} - \frac{1}{20}\right) \).

الخطوة 2: تُختصر جميع الحدود الوسطى ولا يتبقى سوى الحد الأول والحد الأخير: \( \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{20} \).

الخطوة 3: نوحد المقامات ونبسّط الكسر: \( \frac{19}{20} \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: يمكنك تجربة أول حدّين فقط للتأكد فوراً من صحة الاختصار التلسكوبي!

en.question: What is the exact value of the sum \( \frac{1}{2\times3} + \frac{1}{3\times4} + \dots + \frac{1}{21\times22} \)?
en.hint: Rewrite each fraction using 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1) and watch almost every term cancel out!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Use the telescoping identity \( \frac{1}{k(k+1)} = \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \): every inner negative fraction cancels the next positive fraction!

Step 1: Split each term: \( \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\right) + \dots + \left(\frac{1}{21} - \frac{1}{22}\right) \).

Step 2: All middle terms cancel in pairs, leaving only the very first and very last pieces: \( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{22} \).

Step 3: Combine over common denominator \( 44 \) and simplify: \( \frac{5}{11} \).

✅ Quick Check: Test with just 2 terms (\( \frac{1}{2(3)} + \frac{1}{(3)(4)} \)): the formula \( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} \) works identically!

ar.hint: أعد كتابة كل كسر بالمتطابقة 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1) وستلاحظ شطب جميع الحدود الوسطى بالتعاقب!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: نستخدم المتطابقة التلسكوبية \( \frac{1}{k(k+1)} = \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \) حيث يُشطب كل حد سالب مع الحد الموجب الذي يليه!

الخطوة 1: نفكّك كل كسر: \( \left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{5}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{6}\right) + \dots + \left(\frac{1}{39} - \frac{1}{40}\right) \).

الخطوة 2: تُختصر جميع الحدود الوسطى ولا يتبقى سوى الحد الأول والحد الأخير: \( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{40} \).

الخطوة 3: نوحد المقامات ونبسّط الكسر: \( \frac{9}{40} \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: يمكنك تجربة أول حدّين فقط للتأكد فوراً من صحة الاختصار التلسكوبي!

en.question: What is the exact value of \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}} + \dots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{15}+\sqrt{16}} \)?
en.hint: Rationalize the denominator of 1/(√k + √(k+1)) by multiplying top and bottom by (√(k+1) − √k)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Multiply numerator and denominator of \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{k+1}} \) by its conjugate \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \): since \( (\sqrt{k+1})^2 - (\sqrt{k})^2 = 1 \), each fraction becomes simply \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \)!

Step 1: Rewrite every term: \( (\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{1}) + (\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}) + \dots + (\sqrt{16} - \sqrt{15}) \).

Step 2: All intermediate square roots cancel out, leaving \( \sqrt{16} - \sqrt{1} \).

Step 3: Evaluate the exact square roots: \( 4 - 1 = 3 \).

✅ Quick Check: Both \( 16 \) and \( 1 \) are perfect squares (\( 4^2 \) and \( 1^2 \)), giving the clean integer \( 3 \)!

الخطوة 3: نحسب الجذرين التربيعيين: \( 4 - 1 = 3 \).

ar.question: ما القيمة الدقيقة للمجموع \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}+\sqrt{5}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{6}} + \dots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{35}+\sqrt{36}} \)؟
ar.hint: أنطق مقام الحد العام 1/(√k + √(k+1)) بالضرب بسطاً ومقاماً في المرافق (√(k+1) − √k)!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بضرب البسط والمقام للكسر \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{k+1}} \) في المرافق \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \)، يصبح المقام \( (k+1) - k = 1 \)، فيتحول كل حد إلى \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \)!

الخطوة 1: نعيد كتابة المجموع: \( (\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{4}) + (\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{5}) + \dots + (\sqrt{36} - \sqrt{35}) \).

الخطوة 2: تُشطب جميع الجذور الوسطى بالتعاقب ولا يبقى سوى \( \sqrt{36} - \sqrt{4} \).

الخطوة 3: نحسب الجذرين التربيعيين: \( 6 - 2 = 4 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: كلا العددين \( 36 \) و\( 4 \) مربعان كاملان، فيكون الناتج عدداً صحيحاً بسيطاً هو \( 4 \)!

en.question: What is the exact value of \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{10}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{11}} + \dots + \frac{1}{\sqrt{48}+\sqrt{49}} \)?
en.hint: Rationalize the denominator of 1/(√k + √(k+1)) by multiplying top and bottom by (√(k+1) − √k)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Multiply numerator and denominator of \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{k+1}} \) by its conjugate \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \): since \( (\sqrt{k+1})^2 - (\sqrt{k})^2 = 1 \), each fraction becomes simply \( \sqrt{k+1} - \sqrt{k} \)!

Step 1: Rewrite every term: \( (\sqrt{10} - \sqrt{9}) + (\sqrt{11} - \sqrt{10}) + \dots + (\sqrt{49} - \sqrt{48}) \).

Step 2: All intermediate square roots cancel out, leaving \( \sqrt{49} - \sqrt{9} \).

Step 3: Evaluate the exact square roots: \( 7 - 3 = 4 \).

✅ Quick Check: Both \( 49 \) and \( 9 \) are perfect squares (\( 7^2 \) and \( 3^2 \)), giving the clean integer \( 4 \)!

en.question: Consider the product \( 3 \times 5 \times 8 \). You are allowed to add \( 1 \) to exactly one of the three factors. What is the largest possible increase in the value of the product?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 3 \) adds \( 1 \times 5 \times 8 = 40 \); increasing \( 5 \) adds \( 1 \times 3 \times 8 = 24 \); increasing \( 8 \) adds \( 1 \times 3 \times 5 = 15 \).

Step 2: The largest increase comes from adding \( 1 \) to the smallest factor \( 3 \): \( 1 \times 5 \times 8 = 40 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 8 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 15 \)), not the largest!

ar.question: لديك حاصل الضرب \( 3 \times 5 \times 8 \). يُسمح لك بإضافة \( 1 \) إلى عامل واحد فقط من العوامل الثلاثة. ما أكبر زيادة ممكنة في قيمة حاصل الضرب؟
ar.hint: يظن كثير من الطلاب أنه يجب زيادة أكبر عامل! فكّ القوس (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc لتكتشف لماذا العكس هو الصحيح!

الخطوة 1: نقارن الزيادات الثلاث: زيادة \( 3 \) تضيف \( 40 \)، وزيادة \( 5 \) تضيف \( 24 \)، وزيادة \( 8 \) تضيف \( 15 \).

الخطوة 2: أكبر زيادة تنتج من إضافة \( 1 \) إلى أصغر عامل \( 3 \): \( 1 \times 5 \times 8 = 40 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: انتبه للفخ: زيادة أكبر عامل (\( 8 \)) تعطي أقل زيادة (\( 15 \)) وليس أكبرها!

en.question: Consider the product \( 4 \times 7 \times 10 \). You are allowed to add \( 1 \) to exactly one of the three factors. What is the largest possible increase in the value of the product?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 4 \) adds \( 1 \times 7 \times 10 = 70 \); increasing \( 7 \) adds \( 1 \times 4 \times 10 = 40 \); increasing \( 10 \) adds \( 1 \times 4 \times 7 = 28 \).

Step 2: The largest increase comes from adding \( 1 \) to the smallest factor \( 4 \): \( 1 \times 7 \times 10 = 70 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 10 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 28 \)), not the largest!

en.question: Starting with the three numbers \( 5, 8, 12 \), you add \( 1 \) to exactly one of them and then multiply all three numbers together. What is the maximum possible product you can obtain?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 5 \) adds \( 1 \times 8 \times 12 = 96 \); increasing \( 8 \) adds \( 1 \times 5 \times 12 = 60 \); increasing \( 12 \) adds \( 1 \times 5 \times 8 = 40 \).

Step 2: Increasing the smallest factor \( 5 \) to \( 6 \) gives the maximum product: \( 6 \times 8 \times 12 = 576 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 12 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 40 \)), not the largest!

ar.question: لديك الأعداد الثلاثة \( 5, 8, 12 \). إذا أضفت \( 1 \) إلى عدد واحد فقط منها ثم ضربت الأعداد الثلاثة معاً، فما أكبر حاصل ضرب ممكن يمكنك الحصول عليه؟
ar.hint: يظن كثير من الطلاب أنه يجب زيادة أكبر عامل! فكّ القوس (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc لتكتشف لماذا العكس هو الصحيح!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عندما يكون \( a < b < c \)، فإن زيادة \( a \) بمقدار \( d \) تضيف \( d \cdot b c \)، بينما زيادة \( c \) تضيف \( d \cdot a b \) فقط! وبما أن \( b c > a c > a b \)، نزيد دائماً أصغر عامل موجب!

الخطوة 1: نقارن الزيادات الثلاث: زيادة \( 5 \) تضيف \( 96 \)، وزيادة \( 8 \) تضيف \( 60 \)، وزيادة \( 12 \) تضيف \( 40 \).

الخطوة 2: بزيادة أصغر عامل \( 5 \) ليصبح \( 6 \) نحصل على أكبر حاصل ضرب: \( 6 \times 8 \times 12 = 576 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: انتبه للفخ: زيادة أكبر عامل (\( 12 \)) تعطي أقل زيادة (\( 40 \)) وليس أكبرها!

en.question: Consider the product \( 4 \times 9 \times 11 \). You are allowed to add \( 2 \) to exactly one of the three factors. What is the largest possible increase in the value of the product?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 4 \) adds \( 2 \times 9 \times 11 = 198 \); increasing \( 9 \) adds \( 2 \times 4 \times 11 = 88 \); increasing \( 11 \) adds \( 2 \times 4 \times 9 = 72 \).

Step 2: The largest increase comes from adding \( 2 \) to the smallest factor \( 4 \): \( 2 \times 9 \times 11 = 198 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 11 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 72 \)), not the largest!

en.question: Starting with the three numbers \( 3, 8, 14 \), you add \( 2 \) to exactly one of them and then multiply all three numbers together. What is the maximum possible product you can obtain?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 3 \) adds \( 2 \times 8 \times 14 = 224 \); increasing \( 8 \) adds \( 2 \times 3 \times 14 = 84 \); increasing \( 14 \) adds \( 2 \times 3 \times 8 = 48 \).

Step 2: Increasing the smallest factor \( 3 \) to \( 5 \) gives the maximum product: \( 5 \times 8 \times 14 = 560 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 14 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 48 \)), not the largest!

en.question: Consider the product \( 7 \times 11 \times 16 \). You are allowed to add \( 1 \) to exactly one of the three factors. What is the largest possible increase in the value of the product?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!

ar.question: لديك حاصل الضرب \( 5 \times 12 \times 18 \). يُسمح لك بإضافة \( 2 \) إلى عامل واحد فقط من العوامل الثلاثة. ما أكبر زيادة ممكنة في قيمة حاصل الضرب؟
ar.hint: يظن كثير من الطلاب أنه يجب زيادة أكبر عامل! فكّ القوس (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc لتكتشف لماذا العكس هو الصحيح!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: عندما يكون \( a < b < c \)، فإن زيادة \( a \) بمقدار \( d \) تضيف \( d \cdot b c \)، بينما زيادة \( c \) تضيف \( d \cdot a b \) فقط! وبما أن \( b c > a c > a b \)، نزيد دائماً أصغر عامل موجب!

الخطوة 1: نقارن الزيادات الثلاث: زيادة \( 5 \) تضيف \( 432 \)، وزيادة \( 12 \) تضيف \( 180 \)، وزيادة \( 18 \) تضيف \( 120 \).

الخطوة 2: أكبر زيادة تنتج من إضافة \( 2 \) إلى أصغر عامل \( 5 \): \( 2 \times 12 \times 18 = 432 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: انتبه للفخ: زيادة أكبر عامل (\( 18 \)) تعطي أقل زيادة (\( 120 \)) وليس أكبرها!

en.question: Consider the product \( 8 \times 13 \times 20 \). You are allowed to add \( 3 \) to exactly one of the three factors. What is the largest possible increase in the value of the product?
en.hint: Many students guess you should increase the LARGEST factor — expand (a + d)bc = abc + d·bc to see why the opposite is true!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: When \( a < b < c \), increasing \( a \) by \( d \) adds \( d \cdot b c \), whereas increasing \( c \) by \( d \) only adds \( d \cdot a b \). Since \( b c > a c > a b \), always increase the smallest positive factor!

Step 1: Compare the three gains: increasing \( 8 \) adds \( 3 \times 13 \times 20 = 780 \); increasing \( 13 \) adds \( 3 \times 8 \times 20 = 480 \); increasing \( 20 \) adds \( 3 \times 8 \times 13 = 312 \).

Step 2: The largest increase comes from adding \( 3 \) to the smallest factor \( 8 \): \( 3 \times 13 \times 20 = 780 \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap busted: increasing the largest factor \( 20 \) gives the smallest gain (\( 312 \)), not the largest!

en.question: A list of \( 5 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 12 \) and a median of \( 11 \). Two new numbers, \( 8 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 11 \) and the new mean of all \( 7 \) numbers becomes \( 14 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 5×12, new sum = 7×14!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 5 \) numbers: \( 5 \times 12 = 60 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 7 \) numbers: \( 7 \times 14 = 98 \).

Step 3: So \( 8 + y = 98 - 60 = 38 \implies y = 38 - 8 = 30 \) (and since \( 8 < 11 < 30 \), the median indeed stays \( 11 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{60 + 8 + 30}{7} = \frac{98}{7} = 14 \).

ar.question: قائمة مكوّنة من \( 5 \) أعداد متوسطها الحسابي \( 12 \) ووسيطها \( 11 \). أُضيف عددان جديدان هما \( 8 \) و\( y \) إلى القائمة. إذا بقي الوسيط \( 11 \) وأصبح المتوسط الحسابي الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 7 \) يساوي \( 14 \)، فما قيمة \( y \)؟
ar.hint: حوّل المتوسطين إلى مجموعين كليين: المجموع الأصلي = 5×12، والمجموع الجديد = 7×14!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: إضافة عدد أصغر من الوسيط وعدد أكبر من الوسيط يحافظ على موقع الوسيط ثابتاً، بينما يحدد المجموع الكلي قيمة \( y \)!

en.question: A list of \( 6 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 15 \) and a median of \( 14 \). Two new numbers, \( 10 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 14 \) and the new mean of all \( 8 \) numbers becomes \( 17 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 6×15, new sum = 8×17!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 6 \) numbers: \( 6 \times 15 = 90 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 8 \) numbers: \( 8 \times 17 = 136 \).

Step 3: So \( 10 + y = 136 - 90 = 46 \implies y = 46 - 10 = 36 \) (and since \( 10 < 14 < 36 \), the median indeed stays \( 14 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{90 + 10 + 36}{8} = \frac{136}{8} = 17 \).

en.question: A list of \( 7 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 20 \) and a median of \( 19 \). Two new numbers, \( 15 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 19 \) and the new mean of all \( 9 \) numbers becomes \( 22 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 7×20, new sum = 9×22!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 7 \) numbers: \( 7 \times 20 = 140 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 9 \) numbers: \( 9 \times 22 = 198 \).

Step 3: So \( 15 + y = 198 - 140 = 58 \implies y = 58 - 15 = 43 \) (and since \( 15 < 19 < 43 \), the median indeed stays \( 19 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{140 + 15 + 43}{9} = \frac{198}{9} = 22 \).

en.question: A list of \( 8 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 18 \) and a median of \( 18 \). Two new numbers, \( 12 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 18 \) and the new mean of all \( 10 \) numbers becomes \( 21 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 8×18, new sum = 10×21!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 8 \) numbers: \( 8 \times 18 = 144 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 10 \) numbers: \( 10 \times 21 = 210 \).

Step 3: So \( 12 + y = 210 - 144 = 66 \implies y = 66 - 12 = 54 \) (and since \( 12 < 18 < 54 \), the median indeed stays \( 18 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{144 + 12 + 54}{10} = \frac{210}{10} = 21 \).

الخطوة 2: المجموع الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 10 \): \( 10 \times 21 = 210 \).

الخطوة 3: إذن \( 12 + y = 210 - 144 = 66 \implies y = 54 \) (وبما أن \( 12 < 18 < 54 \) يبقى الوسيط \( 18 \) كما هو!).

en.question: A list of \( 9 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 25 \) and a median of \( 24 \). Two new numbers, \( 20 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 24 \) and the new mean of all \( 11 \) numbers becomes \( 27 \), what is \( y \)?

en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 11 \) numbers: \( 11 \times 27 = 297 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{225 + 20 + 52}{11} = \frac{297}{11} = 27 \).

en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 10×30, new sum = 12×33!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 10 \) numbers: \( 10 \times 30 = 300 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 12 \) numbers: \( 12 \times 33 = 396 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{300 + 22 + 74}{12} = \frac{396}{12} = 33 \).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{420 + 28 + 84}{14} = \frac{532}{14} = 38 \).

ar.question: قائمة مكوّنة من \( 12 \) أعداد متوسطها الحسابي \( 35 \) ووسيطها \( 34 \). أُضيف عددان جديدان هما \( 28 \) و\( y \) إلى القائمة. إذا بقي الوسيط \( 34 \) وأصبح المتوسط الحسابي الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 14 \) يساوي \( 38 \)، فما قيمة \( y \)؟
ar.hint: حوّل المتوسطين إلى مجموعين كليين: المجموع الأصلي = 12×35، والمجموع الجديد = 14×38!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: إضافة عدد أصغر من الوسيط وعدد أكبر من الوسيط يحافظ على موقع الوسيط ثابتاً، بينما يحدد المجموع الكلي قيمة \( y \)!

الخطوة 1: المجموع الأصلي للأعداد الـ \( 12 \): \( 12 \times 35 = 420 \).

الخطوة 2: المجموع الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 14 \): \( 14 \times 38 = 532 \).

الخطوة 3: إذن \( 28 + y = 532 - 420 = 112 \implies y = 84 \) (وبما أن \( 28 < 34 < 84 \) يبقى الوسيط \( 34 \) كما هو!).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق: \( \frac{420 + 28 + 84}{14} = 38 \) بالضبط.

en.question: A list of \( 13 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 40 \) and a median of \( 39 \). Two new numbers, \( 31 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 39 \) and the new mean of all \( 15 \) numbers becomes \( 43 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 13×40, new sum = 15×43!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 13 \) numbers: \( 13 \times 40 = 520 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 15 \) numbers: \( 15 \times 43 = 645 \).

Step 3: So \( 31 + y = 645 - 520 = 125 \implies y = 125 - 31 = 94 \) (and since \( 31 < 39 < 94 \), the median indeed stays \( 39 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{520 + 31 + 94}{15} = \frac{645}{15} = 43 \).

en.question: A list of \( 14 \) numbers has a mean (average) of \( 50 \) and a median of \( 48 \). Two new numbers, \( 40 \) and \( y \), are added to the list. If the median remains \( 48 \) and the new mean of all \( 16 \) numbers becomes \( 54 \), what is \( y \)?
en.hint: Convert both averages into TOTAL SUMS: original sum = 14×50, new sum = 16×54!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Adding one number below the median and one number above the median keeps the middle position unchanged, while the total sum determines \( y \)!

Step 1: Original total sum of the \( 14 \) numbers: \( 14 \times 50 = 700 \).

Step 2: New total sum of all \( 16 \) numbers: \( 16 \times 54 = 864 \).

Step 3: So \( 40 + y = 864 - 700 = 164 \implies y = 164 - 40 = 124 \) (and since \( 40 < 48 < 124 \), the median indeed stays \( 48 \)!).

✅ Quick Check: Check: \( \frac{700 + 40 + 124}{16} = \frac{864}{16} = 54 \).

ar.question: قائمة مكوّنة من \( 14 \) أعداد متوسطها الحسابي \( 50 \) ووسيطها \( 48 \). أُضيف عددان جديدان هما \( 40 \) و\( y \) إلى القائمة. إذا بقي الوسيط \( 48 \) وأصبح المتوسط الحسابي الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 16 \) يساوي \( 54 \)، فما قيمة \( y \)؟
ar.hint: حوّل المتوسطين إلى مجموعين كليين: المجموع الأصلي = 14×50، والمجموع الجديد = 16×54!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: إضافة عدد أصغر من الوسيط وعدد أكبر من الوسيط يحافظ على موقع الوسيط ثابتاً، بينما يحدد المجموع الكلي قيمة \( y \)!

الخطوة 1: المجموع الأصلي للأعداد الـ \( 14 \): \( 14 \times 50 = 700 \).

الخطوة 2: المجموع الجديد للأعداد الـ \( 16 \): \( 16 \times 54 = 864 \).

الخطوة 3: إذن \( 40 + y = 864 - 700 = 164 \implies y = 124 \) (وبما أن \( 40 < 48 < 124 \) يبقى الوسيط \( 48 \) كما هو!).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق: \( \frac{700 + 40 + 124}{16} = 54 \) بالضبط.

en.question: Let \( r \) and \( t \) be the two real roots of the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0 \). What is the value of \( r^2 + t^2 \)?
en.hint: Don't use the quadratic formula! In x² − 5x + 3 = 0, the sum of roots is r + t = 5 and the product is r·t = 3!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: For any quadratic \( x^2 - sx + p = 0 \) with roots \( r, t \), expanding \( (x - r)(x - t) = x^2 - (r+t)x + rt \) shows \( r + t = s \) and \( rt = p \).

Step 1: By Vieta's formulas on \( x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0 \), the sum of roots is \( r + t = 5 \) and the product is \( rt = 3 \).

Step 2: Use the identity \( r^2 + t^2 = (r + t)^2 - 2rt \).

Step 3: Substitute: \( (5)^2 - 2(3) = 25 - 6 = 19 \).

✅ Quick Check: Discriminant check: \( 5^2 - 4(3) = 13 > 0 \), confirming both roots are real.

ar.question: ليكن \( r \) و\( t \) الجذرين الحقيقيين للمعادلة التربيعية \( x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0 \). ما قيمة المقدار \( (r - t)^2 \)؟
ar.hint: لا تحل بالقانون العام للجذور! في المعادلة x² − 9x + 14 = 0، مجموع الجذرين r + t = 9 وحاصل ضربهما r·t = 14!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: لأي معادلة تربيعية \( x^2 - sx + p = 0 \) جذراها \( r, t \)، فكّ القوسين \( (x - r)(x - t) \) يبيّن أن \( r + t = s \) و\( rt = p \).

الخطوة 1: من علاقات فييت: \( r + t = 9 \) و\( rt = 14 \).

الخطوة 2: نلاحظ المتطابقة: \( (r - t)^2 = (r + t)^2 - 4rt \).

الخطوة 3: نعوض: \( (9)^2 - 4(14) = 81 - 56 = 25 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق من المميز: \( 9^2 - 4(14) = 25 > 0 \)، فالجذران حقيقيان.

en.question: Let \( r \) and \( t \) be the two real roots of the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 11x + 15 = 0 \). What is the value of \( r^2 + t^2 \)?
en.hint: Don't use the quadratic formula! In x² − 11x + 15 = 0, the sum of roots is r + t = 11 and the product is r·t = 15!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: For any quadratic \( x^2 - sx + p = 0 \) with roots \( r, t \), expanding \( (x - r)(x - t) = x^2 - (r+t)x + rt \) shows \( r + t = s \) and \( rt = p \).

Step 1: By Vieta's formulas on \( x^2 - 11x + 15 = 0 \), the sum of roots is \( r + t = 11 \) and the product is \( rt = 15 \).

Step 2: Use the identity \( r^2 + t^2 = (r + t)^2 - 2rt \).

Step 3: Substitute: \( (11)^2 - 2(15) = 121 - 30 = 91 \).

✅ Quick Check: Discriminant check: \( 11^2 - 4(15) = 61 > 0 \), confirming both roots are real.

en.question: Without a calculator, find the exact value of \( \frac{2026^3 - 26^3}{2026^2 + 2026\times26 + 26^2} \).
en.hint: Replace 2026 with 'a' and 26 with 'b' — recognize the classic cube factorization a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Never cube big numbers by hand in KMC! Let \( a = 2026 \) and \( b = 26 \) and apply \( a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) \).

Step 1: Factor the numerator: the quadratic factor in the denominator cancels out completely!

Step 2: The entire fraction simplifies to \( a - b \).

Step 3: Compute: \( 2026 - 26 = 2000 \).

✅ Quick Check: Test on tiny numbers like \( a=3, b=1 \): \( \frac{27 - 1}{9 + 3 + 1} = 2 \) — works every time!

en.hint: Replace 300 with 'a' and 120 with 'b' — recognize the classic cube factorization a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)!

💡 Key Idea: Never cube big numbers by hand in KMC! Let \( a = 300 \) and \( b = 120 \) and apply \( a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) \).

en.hint: Replace 2026 with 'a' and 1026 with 'b' — recognize the classic cube factorization a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)!

en.question: Without a calculator, find the exact value of \( \frac{5000^3 - 2974^3}{5000^2 + 5000\times2974 + 2974^2} \).
en.hint: Replace 5000 with 'a' and 2974 with 'b' — recognize the classic cube factorization a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Never cube big numbers by hand in KMC! Let \( a = 5000 \) and \( b = 2974 \) and apply \( a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) \).

Step 1: Factor the numerator: the quadratic factor in the denominator cancels out completely!

Step 2: The entire fraction simplifies to \( a - b \).

Step 3: Compute: \( 5000 - 2974 = 2026 \).

✅ Quick Check: Test on tiny numbers like \( a=3, b=1 \): \( \frac{27 - 1}{9 + 3 + 1} = 2 \) — works every time!

en.question: Let \( f(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx + 10 \), where \( a, b, c \) are real constants. If \( f(3) = 28 \), what is the value of \( f(-3) \)?
en.hint: Every exponent of x (5, 3, and 1) is ODD! Replacing x with −x flips the sign of (ax⁵ + bx³ + cx)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Because \( (-x)^5 = -x^5 \), \( (-x)^3 = -x^3 \), and \( (-x)^1 = -x \), the odd-power block \( g(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx \) reverses sign at \( -x \): \( g(-x) = -g(x) \)!

Step 1: From \( f(3) = g(3) + (10) = 28 \), isolate the odd part: \( g(3) = 28 - (10) = 18 \).

Step 2: Flip the input sign: \( g(-3) = -g(3) = -18 \).

Step 3: Add the constant \( 10 \) back: \( f(-3) = -18 + (10) = -8 \).

✅ Quick Check: Shortcut check: \( f(3) + f(-3) = 28 + (-8) = 20 = 2 \times (10) \)!

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بما أن الأسس 5 و3 و1 كلها فردية، فإن الجزء الفردي \( g(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx \) يحقق \( g(-x) = -g(x) \)!

en.question: Let \( f(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx + 12 \), where \( a, b, c \) are real constants. If \( f(5) = 40 \), what is the value of \( f(-5) \)?
en.hint: Every exponent of x (5, 3, and 1) is ODD! Replacing x with −x flips the sign of (ax⁵ + bx³ + cx)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Because \( (-x)^5 = -x^5 \), \( (-x)^3 = -x^3 \), and \( (-x)^1 = -x \), the odd-power block \( g(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx \) reverses sign at \( -x \): \( g(-x) = -g(x) \)!

Step 1: From \( f(5) = g(5) + (12) = 40 \), isolate the odd part: \( g(5) = 40 - (12) = 28 \).

Step 2: Flip the input sign: \( g(-5) = -g(5) = -28 \).

Step 3: Add the constant \( 12 \) back: \( f(-5) = -28 + (12) = -16 \).

✅ Quick Check: Shortcut check: \( f(5) + f(-5) = 40 + (-16) = 24 = 2 \times (12) \)!

ar.hint: جميع أسس x (وهي 5 و3 و1) فردية! استبدال x بـ (−x) يعكس إشارة المقدار (ax⁵ + bx³ + cx) بالكامل!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: بما أن الأسس 5 و3 و1 كلها فردية، فإن الجزء الفردي \( g(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx \) يحقق \( g(-x) = -g(x) \)!

الخطوة 1: من المعطى \( f(8) = g(8) + (14) = 50 \) نوجد قيمة الجزء الفردي: \( g(8) = 50 - (14) = 36 \).

الخطوة 2: عند عكس إشارة المدخل تنعكس إشارة الجزء الفردي: \( g(-8) = -36 \).

الخطوة 3: نضيف الحد الثابت \( 14 \): \( f(-8) = -36 + (14) = -22 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق سريع: مجموع القيمتين \( f(8) + f(-8) = 50 + (-22) = 28 \) وهو ضعف الحد الثابت!

en.question: Let \( f(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx - 8 \), where \( a, b, c \) are real constants. If \( f(9) = 12 \), what is the value of \( f(-9) \)?
en.hint: Every exponent of x (5, 3, and 1) is ODD! Replacing x with −x flips the sign of (ax⁵ + bx³ + cx)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Because \( (-x)^5 = -x^5 \), \( (-x)^3 = -x^3 \), and \( (-x)^1 = -x \), the odd-power block \( g(x) = ax^5 + bx^3 + cx \) reverses sign at \( -x \): \( g(-x) = -g(x) \)!

Step 1: From \( f(9) = g(9) + (-8) = 12 \), isolate the odd part: \( g(9) = 12 - (-8) = 20 \).

Step 2: Flip the input sign: \( g(-9) = -g(9) = -20 \).

Step 3: Add the constant \( -8 \) back: \( f(-9) = -20 + (-8) = -28 \).

✅ Quick Check: Shortcut check: \( f(9) + f(-9) = 12 + (-28) = -16 = 2 \times (-8) \)!

en.question: How many integers \( x \) satisfy \( |x + 2| + |x - 5| = 7 \)?
en.hint: Geometric meaning: |x − (-2)| + |x − 5| is the sum of distances from x to -2 and to 5 on the number line!

en.question: How many integers \( x \) satisfy \( |x - 0| + |x - 11| = 11 \)?
en.hint: Geometric meaning: |x − (0)| + |x − 11| is the sum of distances from x to 0 and to 11 on the number line!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Interpreting \( |x - p| \) as distance on a number line solves absolute-value sums without tedious sign cases!

Step 1: On the number line, the distance between \( 0 \) and \( 11 \) is \( 11 - (0) = 11 \).

Step 2: For ANY point \( x \) between \( 0 \) and \( 11 \) (inclusive), the sum of its distances to the two endpoints equals the full segment length \( 11 \)!

Step 3: Count all integers from \( 0 \) to \( 11 \) inclusive: \( 11 - (0) + 1 = 12 \).

✅ Quick Check: Classic trap avoided: when \( c = b - a \), there isn't just 2 solutions — the entire interval \( [0, 11] \) works!

en.question: A cube of edge length \( 2 \) cm is inscribed inside the smallest possible right circular cylinder (the four top vertices lie on the top rim and the four bottom vertices lie on the bottom rim, as shown). What is the volume of the cylinder (in \( \text{cm}^3 \))?
en.hint: Look from directly above! The top square of side a is inscribed in the circular base, so the circle's DIAMETER equals the square's DIAGONAL a√2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Top-down view secret: when a square of side \( a \) is inscribed in a circle, the square's diagonal \( a\sqrt{2} \) is the circle's diameter!

Step 1: By the Pythagorean theorem on the top face, diagonal \( d = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2} \) cm.

Step 2: So the cylinder's radius is \( r = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} \), which means \( r^2 = \frac{2 \times 4}{4} = 2 \), and height \( h = 2 \).

Step 3: Cylinder volume: \( V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{4}{2}\right)(2) = 4\pi \).

✅ Quick Check: Since \( \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57 > 1 \), the cylinder volume \( 4\pi \) is strictly greater than the cube volume \( 8 \)!

ar.hint: انظر للشكل من الأعلى! الوجه العلوي للمكعب (مربع ضلعه a) محاط بدائرة القاعدة، لذا فإن قطر الدائرة يساوي قطر المربع a√2!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: سر المسقط العلوي: عندما يُحاط مربع ضلعه \( a \) بدائرة، فإن قطر المربع \( a\sqrt{2} \) هو نفسه قطر الدائرة!

en.question: A cube of edge length \( 4 \) cm is inscribed inside the smallest possible right circular cylinder (the four top vertices lie on the top rim and the four bottom vertices lie on the bottom rim, as shown). What is the volume of the cylinder (in \( \text{cm}^3 \))?
en.hint: Look from directly above! The top square of side a is inscribed in the circular base, so the circle's DIAMETER equals the square's DIAGONAL a√2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Top-down view secret: when a square of side \( a \) is inscribed in a circle, the square's diagonal \( a\sqrt{2} \) is the circle's diameter!

Step 1: By the Pythagorean theorem on the top face, diagonal \( d = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = 4\sqrt{2} \) cm.

Step 2: So the cylinder's radius is \( r = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} \), which means \( r^2 = \frac{2 \times 16}{4} = 8 \), and height \( h = 4 \).

Step 3: Cylinder volume: \( V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{16}{2}\right)(4) = 32\pi \).

✅ Quick Check: Since \( \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57 > 1 \), the cylinder volume \( 32\pi \) is strictly greater than the cube volume \( 64 \)!

en.question: A cube of edge length \( 2 \) cm fits tightly inside a right circular cylinder of height \( 2 \) cm, with all \( 8 \) vertices touching the circular rims as shown. What is the volume of the empty space inside the cylinder outside the cube?
en.hint: Look from directly above! The top square of side a is inscribed in the circular base, so the circle's DIAMETER equals the square's DIAGONAL a√2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Top-down view secret: when a square of side \( a \) is inscribed in a circle, the square's diagonal \( a\sqrt{2} \) is the circle's diameter!

Step 1: By the Pythagorean theorem on the top face, diagonal \( d = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2} \) cm.

Step 2: So the cylinder's radius is \( r = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} \), which means \( r^2 = \frac{2 \times 4}{4} = 2 \), and height \( h = 2 \).

ar.question: يستقر مكعب طول حرفه \( 2 \) سم بإحكام داخل أسطوانة دائرية قائمة ارتفاعها \( 2 \) سم بحيث تمس رؤوسه الثمانية حافتي القاعدتين كما في الشكل. ما حجم الفراغ المتبقي داخل الأسطوانة خارج المكعب؟

💡 الفكرة الأساسية: سر المسقط العلوي: عندما يُحاط مربع ضلعه \( a \) بدائرة، فإن قطر المربع \( a\sqrt{2} \) هو نفسه قطر الدائرة!

en.question: A cube of edge length \( 4 \) cm fits tightly inside a right circular cylinder of height \( 4 \) cm, with all \( 8 \) vertices touching the circular rims as shown. What is the volume of the empty space inside the cylinder outside the cube?
en.hint: Look from directly above! The top square of side a is inscribed in the circular base, so the circle's DIAMETER equals the square's DIAGONAL a√2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Top-down view secret: when a square of side \( a \) is inscribed in a circle, the square's diagonal \( a\sqrt{2} \) is the circle's diameter!

Step 1: By the Pythagorean theorem on the top face, diagonal \( d = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = 4\sqrt{2} \) cm.

Step 2: So the cylinder's radius is \( r = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} \), which means \( r^2 = \frac{2 \times 16}{4} = 8 \), and height \( h = 4 \).

Step 3: Subtract the cube volume \( 4^3 = 64 \) from the cylinder volume \( 32\pi \): \( 32\pi - 64 \).

✅ Quick Check: Since \( \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57 > 1 \), the cylinder volume \( 32\pi \) is strictly greater than the cube volume \( 64 \)!

ar.question: يستقر مكعب طول حرفه \( 8 \) سم بإحكام داخل أسطوانة دائرية قائمة ارتفاعها \( 8 \) سم بحيث تمس رؤوسه الثمانية حافتي القاعدتين كما في الشكل. ما حجم الفراغ المتبقي داخل الأسطوانة خارج المكعب؟
ar.hint: انظر للشكل من الأعلى! الوجه العلوي للمكعب (مربع ضلعه a) محاط بدائرة القاعدة، لذا فإن قطر الدائرة يساوي قطر المربع a√2!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: سر المسقط العلوي: عندما يُحاط مربع ضلعه \( a \) بدائرة، فإن قطر المربع \( a\sqrt{2} \) هو نفسه قطر الدائرة!

الخطوة 1: من فيثاغورس على المربع العلوي، طول القطر \( d = 8\sqrt{2} \) سم.

الخطوة 2: إذن نصف قطر قاعدة الأسطوانة \( r = \frac{8\sqrt{2}}{2} \)، ومنه \( r^2 = 32 \)، وارتفاعها \( h = 8 \).

en.question: A cube of edge length \( 10 \) cm is inscribed inside the smallest possible right circular cylinder (the four top vertices lie on the top rim and the four bottom vertices lie on the bottom rim, as shown). What is the volume of the cylinder (in \( \text{cm}^3 \))?
en.hint: Look from directly above! The top square of side a is inscribed in the circular base, so the circle's DIAMETER equals the square's DIAGONAL a√2!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Top-down view secret: when a square of side \( a \) is inscribed in a circle, the square's diagonal \( a\sqrt{2} \) is the circle's diameter!

Step 1: By the Pythagorean theorem on the top face, diagonal \( d = \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = 10\sqrt{2} \) cm.

Step 2: So the cylinder's radius is \( r = \frac{10\sqrt{2}}{2} \), which means \( r^2 = \frac{2 \times 100}{4} = 50 \), and height \( h = 10 \).

Step 3: Cylinder volume: \( V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{100}{2}\right)(10) = 500\pi \).

✅ Quick Check: Since \( \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57 > 1 \), the cylinder volume \( 500\pi \) is strictly greater than the cube volume \( 1000 \)!

ar.question: يستقر مكعب طول حرفه \( 10 \) سم بإحكام داخل أسطوانة دائرية قائمة ارتفاعها \( 10 \) سم بحيث تمس رؤوسه الثمانية حافتي القاعدتين كما في الشكل. ما حجم الفراغ المتبقي داخل الأسطوانة خارج المكعب؟
ar.hint: انظر للشكل من الأعلى! الوجه العلوي للمكعب (مربع ضلعه a) محاط بدائرة القاعدة، لذا فإن قطر الدائرة يساوي قطر المربع a√2!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: سر المسقط العلوي: عندما يُحاط مربع ضلعه \( a \) بدائرة، فإن قطر المربع \( a\sqrt{2} \) هو نفسه قطر الدائرة!

الخطوة 1: من فيثاغورس على المربع العلوي، طول القطر \( d = 10\sqrt{2} \) سم.

الخطوة 2: إذن نصف قطر قاعدة الأسطوانة \( r = \frac{10\sqrt{2}}{2} \)، ومنه \( r^2 = 50 \)، وارتفاعها \( h = 10 \).

الخطوة 3: نطرح حجم المكعب \( 10^3 = 1000 \) من حجم الأسطوانة \( 500\pi \): \( 500\pi - 1000 \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: بما أن \( \frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57 > 1 \)، فإن حجم الأسطوانة أكبر فعلاً من حجم المكعب!

en.question: In isosceles triangle \( ABC \) with \( AB = BC \) and \( \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 37^\circ \), point \( P \) lies inside \( \triangle ABC \) and point \( Q \) lies on segment \( PC \) such that \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) (with \( A \leftrightarrow C \), \( P \leftrightarrow P \), \( Q \leftrightarrow B \)). What is the measure of \( \angle AQC \)?
en.hint: Match corresponding sides & angles carefully: AP = CP puts P on the symmetry line through B, and ∠APQ = ∠CPB around P makes all three angles at P equal 120°!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: From \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \), we get \( AP = CP \) and \( \angle APQ = \angle CPB \). Since \( AB = CB \) and \( AP = CP \), line \( BP \) is the axis of symmetry of the figure!

Step 1: In \( \triangle ABC \), \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 2(37^\circ) = 106^\circ \). Because \( BP \) bisects \( \angle ABC \), \( \angle CBP = \frac{106^\circ}{2} = 53^\circ \).

Step 2: Since \( Q \) lies on \( PC \), \( \angle APC = \angle APQ = \angle CPB \); by symmetry \( \angle BPA = \angle CPB \) too, so all 3 angles around \( P \) are \( 120^\circ \) and \( \angle PAC = \angle PCA = 30^\circ \).

Step 3: By congruence \( \angle AQP = \angle CBP = 53^\circ \), \( \angle AQC = 180^\circ - 53^\circ = 127^\circ \), and \( \angle PAQ = \angle PCB = 37^\circ - 30^\circ = 7^\circ \) — giving \( \angle AQC = 127^\circ \).

✅ Quick Check: Angle sum check in \( \triangle APQ \): \( 120^\circ + 7^\circ + 53^\circ = 180^\circ \)!

ar.question: في المثلث متطابق الضلعين \( ABC \) حيث \( AB = BC \) و\( \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 37^\circ \)، تقع النقطة \( P \) داخل المثلث وتقع النقطة \( Q \) على القطعة \( PC \) بحيث يتطابق المثلثان \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) (بالتناظر \( A \leftrightarrow C \) و\( P \leftrightarrow P \) و\( Q \leftrightarrow B \)). ما قياس الزاوية \( \angle AQC \)؟
ar.hint: طابق الأضلاع والزوايا المتناظرة: AP = CP يضع P على محور التماثل المار بـ B، وتساوي الزوايا الثلاث حول P يجعل كلاً منها 120°!
ar.explanation:
💡 الفكرة الأساسية: من التطابق \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) نستنتج \( AP = CP \) و\( \angle APQ = \angle CPB \). وبما أن \( AB = CB \) و\( AP = CP \)، فإن المستقيم \( BP \) محور تماثل للشكل!

الخطوة 1: زاوية الرأس \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 2(37^\circ) = 106^\circ \)، وينصّفها \( BP \) فيكون \( \angle CBP = 53^\circ \).

الخطوة 2: بما أن \( Q \) على \( PC \) فإن الزوايا الثلاث حول \( P \) متساوية وتساوي \( 120^\circ \)، ومنه \( \angle PCA = 30^\circ \).

الخطوة 3: من التطابق: \( \angle AQP = \angle CBP = 53^\circ \)، ومكملتها \( \angle AQC = 127^\circ \)، و\( \angle PAQ = 7^\circ \) — إذن \( \angle AQC = 127^\circ \).

✅ التحقق من الحل: تحقق من مجموع زوايا \( \triangle APQ \): \( 120^\circ + 7^\circ + 53^\circ = 180^\circ \)!

en.question: In isosceles triangle \( ABC \) with \( AB = BC \) and \( \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 40^\circ \), point \( P \) lies inside \( \triangle ABC \) and point \( Q \) lies on segment \( PC \) such that \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) (with \( A \leftrightarrow C \), \( P \leftrightarrow P \), \( Q \leftrightarrow B \)). What is the measure of \( \angle AQC \)?
en.hint: Match corresponding sides & angles carefully: AP = CP puts P on the symmetry line through B, and ∠APQ = ∠CPB around P makes all three angles at P equal 120°!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: From \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \), we get \( AP = CP \) and \( \angle APQ = \angle CPB \). Since \( AB = CB \) and \( AP = CP \), line \( BP \) is the axis of symmetry of the figure!

Step 1: In \( \triangle ABC \), \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 2(40^\circ) = 100^\circ \). Because \( BP \) bisects \( \angle ABC \), \( \angle CBP = \frac{100^\circ}{2} = 50^\circ \).

Step 2: Since \( Q \) lies on \( PC \), \( \angle APC = \angle APQ = \angle CPB \); by symmetry \( \angle BPA = \angle CPB \) too, so all 3 angles around \( P \) are \( 120^\circ \) and \( \angle PAC = \angle PCA = 30^\circ \).

Step 3: By congruence \( \angle AQP = \angle CBP = 50^\circ \), \( \angle AQC = 180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ \), and \( \angle PAQ = \angle PCB = 40^\circ - 30^\circ = 10^\circ \) — giving \( \angle AQC = 130^\circ \).

✅ Quick Check: Angle sum check in \( \triangle APQ \): \( 120^\circ + 10^\circ + 50^\circ = 180^\circ \)!

en.question: In isosceles triangle \( ABC \) with \( AB = BC \) and \( \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 44^\circ \), point \( P \) lies inside \( \triangle ABC \) and point \( Q \) lies on segment \( PC \) such that \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) (with \( A \leftrightarrow C \), \( P \leftrightarrow P \), \( Q \leftrightarrow B \)). What is the measure of \( \angle PAQ \)?
en.hint: Match corresponding sides & angles carefully: AP = CP puts P on the symmetry line through B, and ∠APQ = ∠CPB around P makes all three angles at P equal 120°!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: From \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \), we get \( AP = CP \) and \( \angle APQ = \angle CPB \). Since \( AB = CB \) and \( AP = CP \), line \( BP \) is the axis of symmetry of the figure!

Step 1: In \( \triangle ABC \), \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 2(44^\circ) = 92^\circ \). Because \( BP \) bisects \( \angle ABC \), \( \angle CBP = \frac{92^\circ}{2} = 46^\circ \).

Step 2: Since \( Q \) lies on \( PC \), \( \angle APC = \angle APQ = \angle CPB \); by symmetry \( \angle BPA = \angle CPB \) too, so all 3 angles around \( P \) are \( 120^\circ \) and \( \angle PAC = \angle PCA = 30^\circ \).

Step 3: By congruence \( \angle AQP = \angle CBP = 46^\circ \), \( \angle AQC = 180^\circ - 46^\circ = 134^\circ \), and \( \angle PAQ = \angle PCB = 44^\circ - 30^\circ = 14^\circ \) — giving \( \angle PAQ = 14^\circ \).

✅ Quick Check: Angle sum check in \( \triangle APQ \): \( 120^\circ + 14^\circ + 46^\circ = 180^\circ \)!

en.question: In isosceles triangle \( ABC \) with \( AB = BC \) and \( \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 48^\circ \), point \( P \) lies inside \( \triangle ABC \) and point \( Q \) lies on segment \( PC \) such that \( \triangle APQ \cong \triangle CPB \) (with \( A \leftrightarrow C \), \( P \leftrightarrow P \), \( Q \leftrightarrow B \)). What is the measure of \( \angle AQP \)?
en.hint: Match corresponding sides & angles carefully: AP = CP puts P on the symmetry line through B, and ∠APQ = ∠CPB around P makes all three angles at P equal 120°!

Step 3: By congruence \( \angle AQP = \angle CBP = 42^\circ \), \( \angle AQC = 180^\circ - 42^\circ = 138^\circ \), and \( \angle PAQ = \angle PCB = 48^\circ - 30^\circ = 18^\circ \) — giving \( \angle AQP = 42^\circ \).

en.question: Each side of an equilateral triangle \( ABC \) of side length \( 6 \) cm is divided into \( 3 \) equal segments, and lines parallel to the sides partition \( \triangle ABC \) into congruent small triangles, as shown. What fraction of the area of \( \triangle ABC \) is shaded?
en.hint: Dividing each side of a triangle into n = 3 equal parts splits the total area into n² = 9 congruent small triangles (both upright and upside-down)!
en.explanation:
💡 Key Idea: Scaling a triangle's sides by \( 1/3 \) scales area by \( (1/3)^2 = 1/9 \), so \( \triangle ABC \) consists of exactly \( 3^2 = 9 \) equal-area small triangles!

Step 1: Verify by rows from top to bottom: \( 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 \) congruent small triangles.

Step 2: Count the shaded small triangles carefully across the rows: there are \( 3 \) shaded triangles.

Step 3: Form the fraction and simplify: \( \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3} \).

✅ Quick Check: Trap check: don't forget to count BOTH upright and upside-down triangles in the denominator (\( 9 \), not \( 6 \))!
